text: When you pick Platoon or Closers, the players now come filled in for you. Tap anyone to change them.
Platoon calls its fives groups now, not units.
Overtime is now one tap. Near the end of the game, Tied? Add overtime adds it right away, with the same minutes as last time. Tap Change next to it to pick the minutes or who plays.
In Settings, a change to A game now also updates that day’s games you haven’t started.
When you swap a kid, the choices now read For now, Takes their minutes and Sits the rest of the game.
The Next stint button on the bench now just says Next.
The sub interval list now shows only the choices that fit your game’s length.
Under the game’s sentence, a new Who’s here row opens the list of who came.
Swaps you make in a game now count when the next game of the day evens out. A kid who sat out part of game 1 gets that time back in game 2.
A game you already printed now says Changed since printed when its plan has moved. Print it again and the note goes away.
The note about uneven minutes now names every kid who gets a little more and a little less.
The minutes each kid plays now show as a range, like 12–16 min each, under the sentence at the top of a game and on Today.
The Season day chart only says later games even out when they really do, and names the games that do.
New in Order: you can mix the fives. Tap Mix the fives and your stronger players are spread out so every five has some of them.

Order now builds the list for you. The spots that play the most go to your best players, or to the kids furthest behind, whichever you chose for who gets the odd minutes in Settings. Your rules are followed too, and each kid's minutes show beside their name. Move anyone and the list is yours.
When you plan with fixed fives, a later game of the day no longer says it evens out the day. The fives you set decide who plays, so earlier games can’t change that.
Before a game starts, you can copy the rules, how it plans, the format or who’s here from another game. Open Plan and tap Copy from another game.
There is a new way to plan: Order. Put your players in a list and they take turns on the floor in that order. The next game of the day carries on from where the last one stopped.
A kid who shows up late and goes straight onto the floor is still counted as late when you change the plan later. They are owed their share of the time left, not of the whole game.
If a kid shows up late, the time they sit on the bench now counts from when they arrived, not from the start of the game.
Overtime no longer counts toward your limit on how long a kid can sit in a row (Sits at most). A kid who sits at the end of the game and again in overtime is not warned about.
If a kid has a limit on how many minutes they can play and it covers the rest of the quarter or half, changing the plan partway through no longer takes them off before it ends.
After you swap a kid in or out, the plan now warns you if someone sits on the bench more in a row than your Sits at most limit allows.

When your league minimum is in full periods and you change the plan partway through a quarter or half, a kid who has played all of it so far stays on to finish it, and it counts as one of their full periods.
Sitting a kid for the rest of the game, or swapping one in for now, no longer fails when a Plays at most limit is in the way. The plan tells you who ends up over it.
Help, the tour and the About page now use plainer words and shorter sentences.
If Benchcard doesn’t load on a weak connection, it now tries once more by itself. If that fails too, it offers to save your backup and shows a Reload button instead of a blank screen.
New in Settings: you can set the minimum playing time in whole periods. Pick 2, and every kid plays two full periods, start to finish.
New in Settings: make sure every kid gets in at least once each half, or once each quarter.
The limit on how long a kid can play without a rest now shows the time in minutes, so you don’t have to do the math. It also goes higher than before. A break between periods doesn’t count as rest.
If you change the plan during a game, the part already played stays as it was. Only the rest of the game changes.
The plan now warns you if a kid would sit out the whole second half.
When you change the plan mid-game, Benchcard remembers how long each kid has already been on the floor without a rest.
Changing the plan during the last period no longer swaps out the five you picked to start it.
If the five you pick for overtime breaks one of your rules, the plan now tells you.
You can set the minimum playing time as a share of the game, like 25%. A kid who shows up late still gets that share of the time that’s left.
When a kid is missing, mark them Out or Running late. During the game, Benchcard only reminds you about the kids who are running late.
Long names shrink to fit instead of getting cut off. If a name is still too long, it breaks onto a second line with a hyphen.
Your team’s name now sits at the top of the main screen in large type. Tap it to switch teams.
On iPhone, if you added Benchcard to your home screen, Share to print now opens the share menu so you can print the card.
New rule: you can stop a kid from sitting on the bench too long in a row. The old Rest limit is now called Plays at most N in a row.
Bench time is spread out more evenly. A kid who starts, or who has a cap on minutes, no longer sits out a whole half.
When two of your rules can’t both be met, the note under the plan now says which one Benchcard followed.
During the game, who’s coming off and who’s going in stays on screen at every sub, even on a small phone.
When there’s a new version of Benchcard, a message offers to reload. Your game is saved either way.
New printable rotation charts for 6 players, and for games played in two halves.
The first time you open Benchcard, it asks what day your game is. A game you set up the night before now shows the right date on the card.
Screens fit better on small phones and with large text turned on.
If a kid shows up late, you can mark them as here during the game.
Pasting a roster from a list or a spreadsheet now skips the bullet points and the header row.
Game tied at the end? Add overtime during the game, pick who plays, and it prints on the card as OT.
You can now sub four times a period.
